scope: Independent final review of an isolated rendered proposal; no UI edits, commits, deployment or publishing performed by this reviewer.
communicationGoal: Explain why a lab-normal result and a level associated with lower long-term risk may differ, and what EVA adds.
ownerRequest: show me how it would look like and have an independent judge judge the proposal based on the criteria specified before

artifact.en: Many lab reference ranges describe typical results in selected groups of apparently healthy people. They don’t always identify levels linked to lower long-term risk. EVA explains the difference in plain language and puts your results in context with your health history.
artifact.es: Muchos rangos de referencia reflejan resultados habituales en grupos seleccionados de personas aparentemente sanas. No siempre indican qué niveles se asocian a un menor riesgo a largo plazo. EVA explica esa diferencia en lenguaje sencillo y pone tus resultados en contexto con tu historial de salud.
artifact.method: Production-built candidate served through Playwright request fulfillment from local files, synthetic .invalid origin; real app hydrated. No native publication.

independence.disclosure: Text-level judgments were formed and communicated before an agent-status inventory unexpectedly exposed colleagues’ completion summaries. Their reports were not opened and their verdicts were not used as evidence. Rendered judgment is this reviewer's own. This is independent agent review with partial blinding, not human research or human clinician approval.

evidence: CLSI EP28 describes health-associated reference values, reference-subject selection and distinct decision limits; IFCC 2018 distinguishes typical healthy-reference distributions from outcome-associated clinical decision limits.
The exact copy says Many and don’t always, does not say unhealthy-population averages, and uses linked/se asocian rather than causal or treatment promises.
Valley confirms <3.0 mg/L only; its specific derivation remains unknown. AHA confirms hs-CRP lower relative-CVD-risk category <1.0 mg/L, distinct from overall risk.
lenses.smallest_fix: None required to show. Do not present the general paragraph as proof of Valley’s particular cutoff derivation.

evidence: Three sentences establish mechanism, consequence and EVA’s interpretation benefit; there is no new CTA, fear statistic, diagnosis, universal optimum or guaranteed health improvement.
41 English words and 46 Spanish words retain the missing explanation within the existing section.
lenses.qualification: The present-tense health-history product capability is NOT VERIFIED end to end by the preview; it is separately recorded below.

evidence: A simulated novice can now learn why typical reference results and levels associated with lower future risk need not be the same, without opening Sources and context.
The example visibly shows the same 2.9/2,9 mg/L inside the <3 lab reference but outside the <1 lower relative-risk category; the visible overall-risk disclaimer bounds its meaning.
EVA’s stated addition is plain-language interpretation with health history.
lenses.qualification: Agent interpretation only; no human usability study or comprehension rate.

evidence: They has a clear antecedent (lab reference ranges), the sentences progress logically and linked to preserves association.
Selected groups of apparently healthy people is somewhat technical but understandable and medically useful; it is not a reason to remove the explanation.
Muchos / No siempre preserve Many / don’t always; habituales, aparentemente sanas and se asocian preserve the mechanism and claim strength.

Plain-language back-translation: Many reference ranges reflect usual results in selected groups of apparently healthy people; they do not always indicate levels associated with lower long-term risk; EVA explains the difference simply and contextualizes results with health history.
Spain-appropriate analíticas remains in the existing CTA; visible decimal 2,9, operators and units remain intact.
lenses.smallest_fix: None. Historial de salud and pone tus resultados en contexto are understandable; alternate phrasing would be optional polishing.

Published hs-CRP reference <3.0 mg/L, without a stated cutoff derivation.
